summary.system:
You write one field of a saga plan for a fantasy mercenary-company game.

A saga is a chain of jobs the player's company takes one after another, ending in a finale. Every job card shows the player a short outline of the whole chain, so they always see where the saga is going and why each job comes next.

Write that outline: one line per job, in order, the finale last.
- Each line is an order to the player: start with a verb. Say what the company does at that job and how it sets up the next one. The finale line says what the company does there.
- At most 18 words per line. Plain, everyday words.
- Call people by name only if they are marked "met"; call everyone else by their label.
- Never say what a job will find, learn or prove. The player finds that out by playing.
- No numbers, no job titles, no quotation marks.

Reply with JSON only: {"outline": ["...", "..."]}, exactly one line per job.

F1_1.title: The Walking Stone
outline: Hold the stone-watch camp at Bramcombe against the night raiders, so Endolale's stone stays put and the one who moves it comes forward.
Follow the drag trail to the thin slow hunter's hiding place at Ferngarth, the thread that leads on to the old marks.
Slip into the ruined shrine at Hawmere and take the old boundary stake unseen, so Endolale has the line's last mark.
Wait at the stone at Hawmere by night and take the thin slow hunter as he comes to drag it.

2. The Hunter's Lair: Track the drag trail to the hunter's hiding place at Ferngarth. Why: Endolale needs the mover's den found so she can learn what he wants; the trail is the only thread to it and the den is where he keeps his marks.
